newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil rebounds after recent heavy losses.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil rebounds after recent heavy losses.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur fuel oil prices recovered sharply on Wednesday, as talk of end user buying and increased bunker demand added lift to rising crude oil futures, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $96 fob ARA then rose to $99, as bunker demand picked up after a long fallow period. High sulphur cargoes rose by around the same amount, traders said.
Low sulphur prices staged a similar recovery amid talk of sales into Italy. The supposed buyer was not available for comment and dealers differed over the quantities that may have been bought.
February swaps recovered around $5 a tonne and traded at $107 and $107.50 fob NWE. Two refiners offering cargoes earlier in the week were unwilling to discuss their availabilities.

In addition, a French refiner bought a U.K.-origin cargo of low sulphur fuel oil on Tuesday at a confidential floating price. Dealers said this was most likely to cater for increasing inland demand from France.

Demand there has been boosted by recent cold weather as well as a one-day electricity sector strike, which was not expected to result in power cuts but would curtail nuclear power output, French traders said.
